This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 24.05.2022 at about 7.30 p.m. he had been riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA07J3568 near SCCH5 Gangapura Gate, MalurKolar road,
Malur Taluk, Kolar District, a Mahindra Bolero light goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA19C3257 was parked in the middle of the road unmindfully without exhibiting any indicator, parking lights or any signal, due to which he could not able to notice the said goods vehicle due to high beam light emitted by opposite coming vehicles, as a result he dashed against the said goods vehicle, due to the said impact he has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital Kolar, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient, for which he has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.,
3.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: At the time of the accident he was aged about 53 years, hale and healthy, working as vegetable SCCH5 merchant, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., due to this accident he is bed ridden, hence he has has lost his income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.267/2022 is registered against the driver of the said Mahindra Bolero goods vehicle before the Malur Police.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has not appeared, hence placed exparte.
R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying averments of the petition.

The Mahindra Bolero Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA19C3257 was covered by Commercial Vehicle (Goods carrying) package policy vide its No.0708003121P112474925 valid since 12.03.2022 to SCCH5 11.03.2023 and submitted that, petitioner has to prove the insurance policy issued by him.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Further he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 24.05.2022 at about 7.30 p.m. near Gangapura Venkatachalapathi vs S. Abdul Khader on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179057684/

sentences.text: 2 Gate, on MalurKolar Road, Malur Raluk, Kolar District, due SCCH5 to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Bolero Light Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA19C 3257 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined Dr.Imran Hussain, Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW2and
marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, counsel for R2 submitted that, he has no defence evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
SCCH5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.
SCCH5 9.
There is crossexamination by counsel for R2 alleging that, there is no negligency of the bolero jeep driver, only due to negligency of the petitioner this accident is occurred.

Further there is cross examination that, bolero jeep was parked on left side of the road, but such suggestions are denied by the PW1.
10.

Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to 6 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA19C3257 which was parked in middle of the road during night hours without any indication.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence by the R2.
R1 has not at all contested the petition.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of driver of the four wheeler and there is no SCCH 5 negligency of the petitioner.
Further there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident.

11. Further relying on a citation reported in 2023 ACJ 2032 in between Virsa Singh and others V/s.
New India Assurance Co. Ltd., wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India it is held that, 'Negligence Venkatachalapathi vs S. Abdul Khader on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179057684/
3 contributory negligence - motor cycle dashed against a parked truck resulting in death of motor cyclist - High Court held that motor cyclist was negligent to the extent of 60 per cent - pillion rider deposed that accident occurred in night and truck was parked in the middle of road without any indicators - No evidence adduced in rebuttal - Whether High Court erred in holding motorcyclist guilty of contributory negligence - Held: yes'.
12.

Mehboob Ali and Others wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, SCCH5 'Negligence - contributory negligence - leaving vehicle in a dangerous position tribunal and High Court held that, deceased contributed to the accident to the extent of 50 percent Apex Court observed that, accident occurred at night and offending truck was parked in the middle of road without clear indication or signal therefore deceased could not notice the truck and held that truck driver was solely negligent in causing the accident'.
13.

sentences.text: Further relied upon a citation reported in 2019 ACJ 159 in between Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Savita and others wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburgi Bench held that, 'Negligenceleaving vehicle in a dangerous position - motor cycle dashed against a lorry parked in the middle of the road without switching on parking lights resulting in death of motor cyclist - Insurance Company of lorry contended that lorry was parked on the correct side of the road by following traffic rules and abated charge sheet was filed against the deceased which indicates that deceased was at fault and also contributed to the accident - charge sheet was filed against the lorry driver and lorry driver pleaded guilty -

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Savita and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburgi Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: spot panchanama mentions that SCCH5 drier had parked the lorry 2 ft. away from the mid line without switching on parking lights or any other indication - accident occurred during night hours and parking lorry without just cause and without switching on parking lights or any other indication shows negligence on the part of lorry driver - though abated charge sheet was filed against the deceased but records indicate that lorry driver pleaded guilty and has not contested the case -
Whether the tribunal was justified in concluding that accident occurred due to sole negligence of the lorry driver - Held: yes'.

On perusal of the above citations it is clear that, even then it seems that, there is contributory negligence of the mahindra bolero driver, but when bolero is parked during night hours without indication in middle of the road, under such circumstances, there is sole negligency of the bolero driver.
Considering all these aspects, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained type I compound fracture SCCH5 proximal third of shaft of the left tibia (left leg), for which he underwent surgery in the form of closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left proximal tibia and bone grafting and distal locking bolt for left tibia.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summaries are marked as Ex.P.7 issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 24.05.2022 to 28.05.2022, further she took treatment since 31.08.2022 to 03.09.2022.

15. Further Dr.Imran Hussain, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Centre is examined as PW2 and furnished recent clinical examination notes marked as Ex.P.11, evaluation form marked as Ex.P.12, IP card marked as Ex.P.13 and Xray Films are marked as Ex.P.14.

Further Venkatachalapathi vs S. Abdul Khader on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179057684/
4 he has assessed SCCH5 disability for left lower limb at the rate of 36% and whole body disability at the rate of 12%.

16. In crossexamination deposed that, himself and Dr.Devaraj have treated the petitioner, initially surgery is conducted and discharged, again for 3 to 4 times follow up treatment is given, bone grafting is made, extra locking bolt is fixed on left leg.
It is denied that, petitioner has not followed their instructions, so that, 2 nd surgery is made.
As on today fracture is united, petitioner is a vegetable vendor with difficulties he can perform his duties.
Further denied that, petitioner is not suffering from any difficulties and he can do daytoday duties.
Further denied that, in order to help the petitioner, assessed the disability on higher side and deposing false evidence.
SCCH5 17.
Further charge sheet and wound certificate speaks that, it is grievous injury.
Discharge summary speaks that, surgery is conducted on left knee, there was type 1 compound proximal third tibia shaft fracture.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.
Petitioner is aged about 53 years old and he is a vegetable vendor.
Whole body disability assessed by the Doctor is at the rate of 12%.
Considering the nature of the injuries, uniting of the fracture, nature of work and age of the petitioner, this tribunal assessed the whole body functional disability at the rate of 10%.

18. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 53 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of driving license marked as Ex.P.8, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 06.10.1968 and the alleged accident is occurred on SCCH5 24.05.2022,
accordingly relying on Ex.P.8 his age is considered about 54 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 11 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 19. As per his case, he was working as vegetable vendor by selling vegetables on pushard, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.
In the case on hand, petitioner is vegetable vendor so that, he comes under the category of formerly groupIV - now unskilled worker category.

Very accident is occurred on 24.05.2022, accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for unskilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to SCCH5 Rs.13,821/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/

5 is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.13,821/ towards SCCH5 loss of income during laid up period.

21.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 1,82,43700 2. Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,38,18100 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 13,82100 period Total 3,79,43900 22.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,79,439/ with SCCH5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

2 3 . I n t h e c a s e o n h a n d , t h o u g h R 2 h a s d e n i e d i s s u a n c e o f p o l i c y b e a r i n g No.0708003121P112474925 which is valid for the period from 12.03.2022 to 11.03.2023, which is in existence as on the date of accident, but there is no defence evidence in this regard
it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
So that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH5 ::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
